label: end of long input: <DEL> in c-initial sequences, or late b
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.007% of steps) that fires only near the end of the original input of long sequences (L 7-9, t 6-9). It never fires in the copy phase or before step 5. It has two parts: (1) the <DEL> step (about 47% of activation mass), almost always in sequences whose first token is c (first_tok=c carries 81% of mass); (2) late original positions (orig_idx 6-8, rate highest at the final original token), mostly when the input is b (32% of mass), often right after q or f. Activations are largest when the sequence also contains several of z/e/f/m/q (top example: c m z e r f q b d <DEL>). The predicate is the union of those two parts. It gets recall ~0.7 and mass recall ~0.75 but precision only ~1%: most long c-initial sequences and most late b inputs do not activate it, and adding context-token conditions raised precision to at most ~13% while costing recall. So the true trigger is a narrower conjunction that this description does not fully capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=c (+5.36), prev_tok=q (+3.30), orig1=m (+2.68), orig0=v (+2.51), phase=0 & in_tok=b (+2.42), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=b (+2.42). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.35), next_out=- (-3.19), orig2=a (-1.71), orig7=- (-1.70).
